transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Laura (Crestwell Head of Data), Ravi (Security Lead), Maya (Eng Manager)

[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Laura: hi, laura here, we own data for crestwell, handling lineage, pii concerns, etc.
[00:12] Ravi: ravi, security and compliance, i'll focus on encryption, kms, audit logs.
[00:18] Maya: maya, platform lead, we'll own the integration and ops.
[00:22] Sofia: great, daniel from redwood se will go deeper on redaction and retention details.
[00:27] Daniel: yeah hey, thanks. real quick agenda: success criteria, what data flows into the model during the POC, how we log/retain prompts, redaction options, and a benchmarking plan.

[02:05] Daniel: to start, can you sketch the POC workload? volume, request shape, sso?
[02:12] Laura: primary use is clinical summarization and triage suggestions. for pilot we'll send about 2k requests/day, avg prompt size 800 tokens incl notes. could spike to 5k/day.

[04:30] Maya: latency goal is sub-1s token-latency for short prompts but overall turnaround under 1.5s, cost target is important too.

[05:10] Daniel: ok, good. on data handling constraints? what is considered PII in your policy?
[05:18] Ravi: anything that identifies a patient—name, MRN, dob, address. We can't ship raw PHI off-prem without a BA agreement and controls.

[06:00] Sofia: for the POC do you prefer Redwood Hosted API or Dedicated/VPC box?
[06:08] Laura: security would prefer dedicated/VPC but we want to understand tradeoffs cause managed is easier.

[07:20] Daniel: tradeoffs: Hosted is fastest to stand up but logs and prompts may be retained for 30 days by default unless redaction or retention policies are enabled; Dedicated (reserved or private) gives you isolation, VPC peering, and customer-managed KMS for encrypting at rest. also we can disable prompt retention for POC.

[08:50] Ravi: when you say disable prompt retention, do you mean we can prevent storing the raw input anywhere? we still need traces for debugging but only metadata or hashed tokens.

[09:15] Daniel: yes, options are: 1) no prompt storage — ephemeral processing, no logs containing content; 2) redaction pipeline — scrub PHI before it reaches model, store only redacted prompt; 3) store encrypted prompts with KMS and short retention (e.g., 7 days). note that automatic redaction can miss context, so we recommend a hybrid: redact known PII patterns (MRN, SSN, dates) plus a manual review sample.

[11:40] Laura: manual review for a sample is acceptable. how good is the redaction out of the box? we need metrics.

[12:05] Daniel: our redaction service uses regex + ML entity detection; in our benchmarks it catches ~95% of direct identifiers, but less on implied identifiers. we'll run your sample through it for the POC and produce recall/precision numbers.

[14:20] Maya: about prompt storage — can we store only embeddings or hashes instead of raw text?

[14:35] Daniel: yes, two patterns: store only embeddings (one-way) for similarity features, or store redacted text plus a salted hash of the original prompt. both help debugging while reducing exposure. embeddings are irreversible generally, but ensure your compliance team is ok with that.

[16:00] Ravi: audit logs — we need full request/response metadata, user id, timestamps, model version, and a way to query by request id for audits. can those logs be exported to our SIEM?

[16:20] Daniel: yes, Dedicated + Private support streaming audit logs to your S3 or SIEM via Kinesis/CloudWatch, plus we provide per-request trace ids. Hosted can push logs but you'd rely on redwood-managed retention unless you choose log export.

[18:30] Sofia: success criteria recap — what would make the POC successful?
[18:36] Laura: 1) redaction passes with >95% recall on direct identifiers on our sample; 2) latency and cost targets met under expected load; 3) no unredacted PHI stored; 4) ability to export audit logs to our SIEM.

[19:10] Daniel: noted. benchmarks: we'll run three tests — baseline (no redaction), redaction-in-line, and pre-processing redaction. measure latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, and redaction recall/precision.

[21:00] Maya: timeline — we want the POC in the next two weeks if possible.

[21:20] Daniel: realistic: 2-week pilot: week 1 setup + dry-run with anonymized samples, week 2 live-ish with sampled real data under strict controls, followed by a results review.

[22:45] Ravi: legal — we'll need a temporary DPA and a statement of how long logs are kept during the pilot. can you confirm retention settings?

[23:05] Sofia: yes, for the POC we can set retention to 7 days for encrypted prompts or zero retention (no storage) if you choose ephemeral mode. we'll add that to the runbook.

[25:10] Laura: what about prompt caching / KV cache? could that keep data in memory that is accessible later?

[25:25] Daniel: good point. runtime uses KV cache for generation speed, but it's ephemeral and flushed after the request for ephemeral mode. for Dedicated, we can ensure cache memory is isolated per-tenant and evicted on completion. we can also avoid caching for POC to be safe at cost of throughput.

[27:00] Maya: any impact to latency if we enable redaction pre-processing?

[27:10] Daniel: redaction adds a small pre-processing step; in our tests inline redaction adds ~40-80ms median per request depending on rule complexity, pre-processing in a separate pipeline can be parallelized to minimize impact. we'll include numbers in the benchmark report.

[29:40] Laura: how do you handle model responses that might inadvertently leak training data or hallucinate PHI?

[29:55] Daniel: we apply response filtering and can set strict prompt/result post-processing rules. also we can pin model versions that have safety layers. for POC we can configure automatic result redaction before it's stored or returned.

[32:15] Ravi: KMS integration — can we bring our own key? HSM?

[32:25] Daniel: Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS; Private supports on-prem HSMs. Hosted can integrate with your KMS but has more constraints. we'll provide the KMS docs.

[34:40] Sofia: crm/tracking question — what's the estimated cost for two-week Dedicated trial for your stated volumes?

[34:55] Daniel: rough ballpark: for 2k-5k req/day with avg 800 tokens, the Dedicated trial estimate is in the Xk/month range — specifics in pricing deck. Sofia will attach a tailored quote.

[36:10] Maya: curious about retention config UI — can we toggle retention per-route?

[36:20] Daniel: yes, per-route retention and per-model policies: you can set prompt retention to none, 7 days, 30 days, and choose redaction policies per route. RBAC restricts who can change policies.

[38:00] Laura: for the audit we'll need an exported sample: could you run a demo export of anonymized logs to our S3?

[38:12] Daniel: sure, we'll include a sample export as part of the benchmark. i'll run your anonymized sample through the pipeline and push a sample to the S3 bucket you provide (or shared staging bucket).

[40:05] Ravi: last thing — are there any known gaps? e.g., phone numbers embedded in text with typos, implied identifiers?

[40:18] Daniel: yes implied identifiers are harder; regex misses typos. we recommend a small manual review loop, and for POC we'll set up sampling at ~1% of requests flagged for manual audit. we can tune rules after the first run.

[42:00] Sofia: recap & next steps: daniel runs redaction benchmark on your anonymized sample, sofia shares SOC2 + pricing + DPA template, laura to send sample data and raji to send compliance questions, schedule deep-dive week of 9/20.

[42:35] Laura: sounds good, thanks all.
[42:38] Ravi: thanks.
[42:40] Maya: thanks.
[42:42] Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email.

References shared during call:
- Benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/crestwell-poc)
- SOC2 summary + KMS guide (link: https://redwood.example.com/security)
